title: POC weekly sync - onboarding & env readiness
summary: Weekly POC check-in focusing on onboarding progress, VPC access, test dataset preparation, and running initial inference benchmarks. Agreement to run a 1-hour throughput test on dedicated pool next week; Redwood to share network diagram and SOC2 docs; customer to provide s3 test data and open firewall rules for peering.
transcript:
00:00 Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll keep to 45, quick intro, maya from redwood, carlos my se, and on the call from nex a health priya ben and samira, uh we're here for the weekly poc sync, onboarding and env readiness.
00:18 Priya: thanks maya, yes we just want to make sure the VPC stuff is on track and we can run the sample workloads, timeline still dec 15 for pilot wrap? that's what execs want, so wanna make progress.
00:30 Maya: right, dec 15 is the target, ok carlos can you run through infra checklist?
00:35 Carlos: yeah um quick status. we sent the peering template, ni— i mean nexus sent back a couple questions, ben answered most but we need the firewall ports, currently waiting on your network team to open 443 and 10250 and the gRPC ports, we also need the IAM role for S3 read only.
00:52 Ben: noted, we had a question on the NAT gateway, do we need egress to redwood-hosted endpoints or is it purely private?
01:00 Carlos: for the Dedicated pilot, the control plane talk is minimal, but the runtime needs to reach redwood's artifact store if you choose our managed images; if you want fully private we can use an offline bundle, that's the private deployment option.
01:18 Priya: I think we prefer VPC peering with minimal egress, company policy prefers no wide egress. Are the audit logs kept locally? we need to confirm retention.
01:27 Maya: yes, for Dedicated the logs can be forwarded to your S3 or a SIEM via our audit export; retention is configurable, standard is 90 days but we can extend. We'll send a doc.
01:36 Samira: quick question about test data, we will provide an s3 bucket with a 10k sample of de-identified clinical notes, do you need any special formatting?
01:44 Carlos: csv or ndjson is fine, just include a text field and an id. For embeddings/batched rerank tests we prefer ndjson, but csv works. Also please avoid rows with PHI, though you said de-identified.
01:58 Ben: we also need to know about encryption, his— KMS integration, is that supported for the Dedicated runtime?
02:06 Maya: yes KMS/HSM integration is supported in Private and Dedicated, you can bring your own key or use redwood-managed keys. We'll attach the KMS integration guide.
02:15 Priya: thanks. can we talk a little about expected latency? our product team needs sub-300ms p95 for single-turn summarization.
02:23 Carlos: okay so single-turn summarization at sub-300ms p95 will be tight on hosted depending on model size, but on Dedicated with the right GPU profile and optimized kernels we can get close. The other lever is quantization and sequence length. If your prompts are short we can meet that. We should run a focused latency bench.
02:41 Samira: that sounds good. what about KV cache, we've seen references to kv cash in older docs— is that the same as KV cache?
02:48 Carlos: yeah sometimes the auto-transcript spells it wrong, it's KV cache, used for long context speedups. We can enable prefix caching for repeated context.
02:56 Maya: action item— we'll run a small benchmark next week. do you want throughput or latency bench?
03:03 Priya: both, but prioritize latency. also can we test on your mid-size model and one distilled variant?
03:10 Carlos: yes we can provide a mid-size open model plus a quantized variant. For throughput we'll do batch sizes 1,4,8. For latency bench we'll keep batch=1 and measure p50/p95/p99.
03:22 Ben: network could add variance, we should do the bench inside the same region via peered VPC to avoid internet noise.
03:29 Maya: agreed. Ben, can you confirm region & CIDR for peering?
03:34 Ben: yes, we'll share the CIDR and the team will open the rules by EOD thursday.
03:40 Priya: next, security review status? we had a list of items from the security questionnaire, where are we on SOC2 docs and penetration testing?
03:48 Maya: we have SOC2 Type II report available, last completed Q2 2026, and pen test summary can be shared redacted. I'll send links to the security pack.
03:56 Samira: great. also, are there RBAC controls in the console for operators?
04:01 Carlos: yes, role-based access, SAML/SSO integration and fine-grained roles. We'll share a screenshot in the setup doc.
04:08 Priya: ok good. any blockers on the onboarding checklist?
04:12 Carlos: main blocker is the peering and the IAM role to read s3. Also we need to confirm which models you'll test so we can pre-stage binaries on the cluster.
04:21 Samira: we'll confirm models today — likely "redwood-m3a" mid-size and a quantized m3a-quant. we'll upload to s3 by tomorrow.
04:29 Maya: perfect. we'll pre-stage on a dedicated pool. Expected time to pull image and warm kv cache is about 10 minutes for mid-size.
04:37 Priya: can we request increased retention for logs for 180 days? compliance requires 180 for some artifacts.
04:42 Maya: yes we'll note that as a request — policy change needs legal, but operationally doable.
04:47 Ben: a couple of nitty gritty items: do we need a jump box for SSH into nodes for debugging? our policy restricts inbound.
04:55 Carlos: for Dedicated we don't ask for inbound SSH; we provide remote diagnostics via logs and support sessions. If you want a support bastion that's an option but not required.
05:03 Maya: ok moving on, let's pick dates for the benchmarking. we're proposing next Tues dec 1 at 10am PT for a 1-hour throughput+latency run, then we'll review results dec 2. Does that work?
05:15 Priya: yes dec 1 works. we'll aim to have s3 test data + firewall rules by EOD nov 30.
05:22 Samira: noted, I'll upload the ndjson to s3 and share path.
05:27 Ben: we'll provision the IAM role tomorrow morning.
05:32 Carlos: i'll prepare the bench scripts and share the runbook, includes perf metrics and collector config. Also note that for fair comparisons we should disable any on-host caching initially.
05:44 Maya: quick note on costs — the dedicated pool will incur a short-term bump during the bench; we'll produce a rough estimate after the test and then we can discuss longer-term reserved capacity.
05:54 Priya: ok that's fine as long as we understand unit costs.
06:00 Maya: any other questions?
06:04 Priya: one more: downtime SLA during pilot, we need at least 99.5% for business-critical flows.
06:11 Maya: for pilot we can commit to 99.5 as a target; enterprise SLA is negotiated with dedicated contracts. I'll flag that with solutions engineering.
06:19 Samira: also, are there any known tokenizer differences between the open model versions? we've had slight tokenization mismatch earlier with other vendors.
06:27 Carlos: we use standard tokenizer for the model family, but small differences can exist between quantized variants; we'll include tokenization checks in the bench.
06:35 Maya: great. recap and next steps: 1) Redwood to send security pack, network diagram, and bench runbook by EOD nov 30; 2) Nexa to open firewall and provide CIDR + IAM role + s3 path by EOD nov 30; 3) bench run dec 1 10am PT; 4) Redwood to pre-stage models and share expected cost estimate post-bench.
07:00 Priya: that works. thanks everyone.
07:08 Maya: thanks, we'll follow up in email with links and the runbook. bye.
next_steps: Redwood to send SOC2 report, pen-test summary, network diagram and bench runbook by 2026-11-30
NexaHealth to provide S3 test data path, CIDR for VPC peering, and create IAM role by 2026-11-30
Run benchmark (latency first, then throughput) on 2026-12-01 10:00 PT
Redwood to pre-stage models and provide preliminary unit cost estimate after bench

Ben Turner: Open firewall rules (443, 10250, gRPC) and share CIDR; due 2026-11-30
Samira Khan: Upload 10k de-identified test ndjson to S3 and share path; due 2026-11-30
